headline: A dated-exception pressure front is moving across compliance, booking, steel and equipment files.
dek: The weather is not one blended score. W29 has separate clocks: Brazil tariffs, USTR proof work, steel quotas, compressed bookings, EU cargo-data quality and long-lead electrical equipment.

zones.name: Brazil tariff clock
zones.operator_meaning: Reuters reported new 25% duties on selected Brazilian furniture, ethanol, machinery, footwear, sugar and other goods from July 22, with exemptions that still require SKU-level review.
zones.watch: Importer notices, exemption status and supplier origin proof before July 22.

zones.name: Forced-labor proof
zones.operator_meaning: USTR hearings ran July 7-9 for proposed action tied to forced-labor import prohibitions across 60 economies; duty families and exemptions require file-level review.
zones.watch: Transcript posting, rebuttal timing, final action and product examples.

zones.name: UK/EU steel
zones.operator_meaning: GOV.UK said UK tariff-free steel quota volumes were cut 51% with a 50% out-of-quota duty; Reuters reported EU duty-free quotas cut 47% to 18.3M metric tons with the same out-of-quota duty.
zones.watch: Product-code fit, quota availability, substitute approval and transitional treatment.

zones.name: North America booking
zones.operator_meaning: NRF/Hackett forecast July covered-port volume at 2.47M TEU, above the May 2022 record; Maersk described frontloaded imports, tight trans-Pacific space and tightening inland capacity.
zones.watch: Reported July TEU, sailing cutoffs, protected-space availability and inland constraints.

zones.name: Europe cargo data
zones.operator_meaning: Maersk Europe flagged ICS2 Release 3 cargo-data requirements alongside Rotterdam heatwave and Antwerp pilot constraints; weak classification or ENS detail can become a hold risk.
zones.watch: Classification completeness, ENS data quality and carrier operational updates.

zones.name: Power equipment
zones.operator_meaning: Reuters/Wood Mackenzie reported generator step-up transformer lead times above 160 weeks in Q1 2026 and high-voltage circuit-breaker lead times at 125 weeks in H2 2025.
zones.watch: Reservation slots, project float, switchgear availability and approval gates.

reference_cards.note: NRF/Hackett covered-port forecast above prior May 2022 record.

reference_cards.note: Generator step-up transformer lead times reported by Reuters/Wood Mackenzie.

operator_translation: Build a dated exception board instead of a weather score. Each station needs a clock, affected family, required file, primary owner, decision and escalation trigger.
operator_watchlist: USTR transcript posting, rebuttal timing and final action.
Brazil July 22 implementation and importer notices.
Clean Drewry WCI lane details and Maersk booking updates.
Port, Descartes or Reuters confirmation of whether July approaches 2.47M TEU.
UK/EU steel quota effects on buyers and product-code decisions.
Transformer, breaker and switchgear lead-time changes.

newsletter_insert.title: Supply Chain Weather
newsletter_insert.headline: Dated-exception pressure front: the clocks matter more than a composite score.
newsletter_insert.body: This week's weather map has six separate stations: Brazil's July 22 tariff date, USTR forced-labor proof work, UK/EU steel quota pressure, compressed North America bookings, EU ICS2 data quality and long-lead electrical equipment. They should not be blended into one risk number because each has a different owner and clock.
newsletter_insert.operator_translation: Before the next planning meeting, create a dated exception board with one row per trigger: affected family, required file, owner, deadline, decision and escalation trigger.

sources: USTR July and June 2026 forced-labor Section 301 releases
